To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the mutation detection rate for pathologic mutations can be substantially raised by applying preselection by micro‐satellite analysis in HNPCC families; (2) in German HNPCC families, large genomic deletions in MMR genes account for about 10%; (3) in MSH2, the mutation c.942+3a>T accounts for about 11% and in MLH1, the mutation c1489_1491insC for about 18% of
56% of the index patients of a large German HNPCC cohort were found to carry a mutation in MSH2 or MLH1.

the detection rate of mutations in MMR genes in patients with HNPCC can be raised from about 50% to more than 90% by applying preselection by micro‐satellite instability analysis and by screening for large deletions.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a new method for the detection of the genetic variation of the genetic variation.
the development and implementation of new methods for the detection and analysis of genetic variation.
the development and characterization of new methods for the analysis of genetic variation in the human genome.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
in the present study, the mutation frequency in the German HNPCC population is 56%, which corresponds well to the results of other studies in the literature.
the mutation detection rates in our study, which were 56% in index cases and 50% in families, are comparable with other published studies and that our findings are in agreement with previous reports.
, although the overall mutation detection rate is high (56% in index patients), it is not possible to identify the majority of HNPC patients based on clinical features only.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the mutation detection rate in HNPCC patients from Germany can be raised substantially from 40% to 56% by preselecting patients for small mutation analysis by microsatellite instability analysis and by applying a mutation analysis strategy that starts with screening for large deletions and common mutations.

the detection of mutations in MMR‐genes in patients with HNPCC can be improved by microsatellite instability screening and the application of a mutation detection strategy based on a preselected set of mutations.
we have identified a large number of novel mutations, which are of importance for mutation detection in the German population.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the majority of patients with HNPCC can be diagnosed by genetic testing.
the mutation detection rate in HNPCC patients can be substantially increased by preselection of patients with MSI‐H tumors.
microsatellite analysis can substantially increase the mutation detection rate, even in patients not fulfilling the strict Amsterdam criteria.
